mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 2008-2023 sample.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for a month, labor market strength is interpreted as a positive signal for corporate earnings growth, driving S&P 500 forward returns upward over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0 and UNRATE remains below for at least one month
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5% but SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, with a t-statistic exceeding 1.5 (sample size 50).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure index by more than 3% in a single quarter indicates excess demand, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX 20-day returns (Spearman's rho < 0.2, p < 0.1) in post-recession data.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% suggests supply-side acceleration that outpaces demand, leading to compression in equity valuations and negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60 months, no instance where INDPRO > 5% growth and SPX 60-day forward returns are positive (max Sharpe ratio < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 4% with CPIAUCSL also above 2% indicate persistent inflationary expectations, which depresses equity discount rates and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% AND CPIAUCSL > 200 (1982=100) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 30 instances meeting the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly PAYEMS below 120,000 suggests soft labor market conditions that reduce earnings growth forecasts and drive negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 10 episodes of PAYEMS < 120000, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (household spending in thousands) rises by more than 10% in a single month, it signals a demand surge that is predictive of strong corporate earnings and positive 60-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: In 15 such spikes since 2000, 60-day forward returns are not outperforming the market benchmark (Merton ratio < 1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 months), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative, regardless of other macro variables.
failure_condition: In 10 tightening regimes since 1980, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
